caption: What if the Moon came twice as close? Right now it sits about 384,400 km away. On 24 November, the Beaver supermoon swings in to about 360,800 km, only around 6% closer, and looks about 6.5% bigger. Now halve the distance to 192,000 km. The Moon would look twice as wide, cover 4 times the area of sky and full-moon nights would be about 4 times brighter. Its tidal pull depends on distance cubed, so the pull on our oceans would be 8 times stronger, and high tides would reach much farther up beaches like Juhu. A closer orbit is also faster: one lap in about 10 days, so roughly 36 Purnimas a year. And it would look twice as wide as the Sun, so no more 'ring of fire' eclipses. Plot twist: the Moon really was closer long ago. It drifts away about 3.8 cm every year, and 1.4 billion years ago a day on Earth lasted just over 18 hours. Would YOU want a giant Moon? 👇
